content.overview: A useful defect record describes what was observed, where, when and at what scale before assigning a cause. Similar appearances can arise from different biological, physical or process mechanisms.

vocabulary.definition: Observed departure from a defined or expected product attribute.
Set of plausible explanations retained until evidence distinguishes them.
Distribution across units, locations or time that informs an investigation.

sections.title: Describe before diagnosing
sections.body: Record color, texture, odor, location, extent and affected units using neutral language. A visual observation alone may not identify a microorganism or process cause.

sections.title: Map the pattern
sections.body: Clustering by rack, container, handling step or time can guide hypotheses and scope without proving root cause.

sections.title: Preserve original records and images
sections.body: Attributable images, sample IDs and controlled corrections protect investigation integrity.

workedExamples: A white deposit is recorded with location, texture and distribution while contamination, residue and plant material remain in the differential.
commonMistakes: Naming a pathogen from appearance alone.
Photographing without lot or scale context.
Editing the original observation after a later diagnosis.
content.practicalApplication: Write an objective defect record and evidence table that separates observations from hypotheses.
content.summary: Neutral description and mapped patterns create stronger investigations than immediate visual diagnosis.
